recent_articles.title: Israel’s October 7 tribunal: Show trial of Palestinians or justice? | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Israel** approved a special military tribunal to try Palestinians accused of participating in the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack.  The tribunal will have the power to impose the death penalty and has drawn criticism from international organizations including the **United Nations**, which called for its repeal. Human rights groups like Amnesty International and B'tselem condemn the legislation as a way of seeking revenge on imprisoned Palestinians, while some Israeli parliamentarians believe it will bring justice. The tribunal is expected to hold televised trials of an estimated 300 detainees, many of whom are civilians, with concerns raised about potential unfair trials due to coercive practices in security-related cases.  The move has been met with mixed reactions, with some Israelis supporting the tribunal while others call for a state commission of inquiry into the government's role in preventing the attack.

recent_articles.title: Drugged, raped and filmed: German woman alleges years of horrific abuse by ex-partner - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **German** woman, 59-year-old Claudia Wuttke, has accused her former partner of drugging and raping her over a period of 16 years, with the alleged crimes captured on video.  Police discovered the videos in June 2025 after finding them on a laptop. The **German** authorities dropped investigations into 65 of the 67 alleged cases due to statute of limitations laws, leaving only two remaining cases for prosecution. Wuttke expressed her disappointment at the lack of justice and called it "unacceptable" that most of the abuse would go unpunished.

recent_articles.title: ‘Kind of humiliating’: trans community responds to EHRC’s new code of practice | Gender | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Stephen Whittle**, a 70-year-old man who advocates for gender recognition, was at the Chelsea flower show when the updated code of practice from the **Equality and Human Rights Commission** was published. The guidance confirmed that single-sex spaces must be used based on biological sex, leading to mixed reactions. Some welcomed it as a consolidation of last year's court victory, while others expressed concern about its practical implications for trans inclusivity.  Businesses and service providers are grappling with the changes, seeking clarity and time to adapt their policies.

recent_articles.title: ‘Most relentlessly cruel’: Gaza flotilla activists tell harrowing accounts of abuse in Israeli custody - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mousa Taher**, a New Zealand activist, and other activists from the Global Sumud humanitarian aid flotilla, recounted harrowing experiences of abuse they endured while detained by **Israeli forces**.  Taher described being subjected to torture, including being bound tightly with plastic zip ties, having his face stepped on, and being beaten. He also said that Israeli soldiers recognized him and addressed him by name because he had previously been detained. **Isselmou Ould Maloum**, a Mauritanian activist, echoed similar accounts of violence, stating that the Israeli military lacks a strategy other than using force against Palestinians.  **Gregory Terry**, an American activist, described the detention as "miserable" and said his fellow activists suffered broken bones and were repeatedly tased. **Juliet Lamont**, an Australian activist, recounted being subjected to sexual assault and physical violence during their time on board the flotilla. All of these activists expressed their determination to continue protesting for Palestinian freedom.

recent_articles.title: Flotilla video: Ben-Gvir’s template of televised abuse was honed on Palestinians | Israel | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Itamar Ben-Gvir**, Israel's national security minister, has been widely criticized for publicly celebrating abuse of detainees in Israeli jails. While **Benjamin Netanyahu**, the Israeli Prime Minister, condemned Ben-Gvir's actions, he has previously failed to address systemic abuse against Palestinians in custody.  This incident highlights a pattern of escalating violence and human rights violations against Palestinians under his leadership, with calls for sanctions and international intervention growing louder.

recent_articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse by Israeli forces while detained

recent_articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege sexual assault and rape in Israeli detention | Israel | The Guardian

recent_articles.title: Ebola risk now at highest level in DR Congo, says WHO - World - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Deepa Jewellers, Cotec Healthcare receive Sebi approval for IPOs - The Economic Times

recent_articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse, sexual assault in Israeli detention | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera

recent_articles.title: Kim Soo-hyun: AI used to fake evidence that ended South Korean actor's career, say police

recent_articles.title: Tanzanian police official Faustine Mafwele sanctioned by US for alleged human rights abuses

recent_articles.title: Boys convicted of rape get non-custodial sentences as judge says they should not be criminalised unnecessarily | UK news | The Guardian

recent_articles.title: Indian-origin truck driver Shamsher Singh jailed for 6 years for raping woman he met on dating app in New Zealand - The Times of India

recent_articles.title: Bolivian president to reshuffle cabinet amid antigovernment protests | Protests News | Al Jazeera

recent_articles.title: Quote of the day by Galileo Galilei: “There are those who reason well, but they are greatly outnumbered by those who reason badly.”

recent_articles.title: 'No evidence you suffered in India': Inside Sanaullah Khan Mohammed's failed attempt to get asylum in US

recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Joseph Vijay**, leader of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), won a significant number of seats in the recent Tamil Nadu election, capitalizing on a sense of restlessness and disillusionment among youth voters.
